Sarah — looping in legal language and a short counterproposal below. Thank you for calling out seasonality; we can accept an averaging approach but need guardrails so the floor doesn't undermine committed economics. Proposed edits:

1) Pricing Floor (proposed new language):
"Exhibit H Section 3(a) Pricing Floor: For the initial twelve (12) month period following the Effective Date, the Customer's billed usage shall be compared to the Customer's committed baseline using a rolling twelve-month average ("Baseline Average"). If the Baseline Average for any measurement period falls below sixty percent (60%) of the committed baseline, Customer shall pay a one-time shortfall true-up equal to the difference between the Baseline Average and sixty percent (60%) of the committed baseline, pro-rated across the twelve (12) month period. Redwood and Customer agree to a thirty (30) day grace window after issuance of the initial invoice to reconcile onboarding timing variance.

Rationale/constraints: the pro-rate language preserves Redwood's committed capacity economics while protecting Brightline from monthly seasonality cliffs.

2) Aggregation for Degression:
"Degression shall be applied on an invoice-level basis unless otherwise expressly stated in the Order Schedule. When multiple SKUs are designated as a single packaged offering in an Order Schedule, the parties may elect to aggregate volumes for the packaged offering by explicit mapping table in Exhibit H. Aggregation without an explicit mapping is disallowed.

3) Packaging rows: we will add three explicit unit rows for the components you listed (Base tokens, Long-context tokens, Embedding units). Redwood will provide a reconciliation table translating the previous blended SKU price into the three line items; any variance that results in a materially lower per-unit price for Customer will be subject to a true-up calculation and a signed amendment.

Attachment: RWI_ExhibitH_countermarkups.pdf (attached) — contains inline edits and redline excerpts.

If this is acceptable in principle we can convert the countermark to a DocuSign-ready order form after the call. If you need alternative floor triggers or a shorter averaging cadence, please propose concrete language and we'll evaluate.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
